_why: ADR 0163's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
The record presented two mutations and was carrying them as prose. This
encodes them so a reader can re-run the claim instead of trusting it --
which is the whole point of ADR 0069's harness, written after the
hand-run one had given a wrong answer three separate ways.
Both mutations target the same line of README.md:
km    0.03 mM    brenda_exact  BRENDA ref 286469
and the argument is that neither is detectable by reading strings.
A. `0.03` -> `0.398`. A REAL value on that BRENDA page -- the other
candidate row, under the same reference. Every string guard passes it,
because 0.398 does occur on the page.
B. `286469` -> `286442`. A REAL lactate dehydrogenase reference. Every
string guard passes it too, because 286442 is a genuine LDH ref.
Only the PAIR is wrong in each case, and only running the resolver can
check a pair. That is the layer ADR 0162 named as open and this one
closed, and it is why the test command below runs the front-page test
rather than any of the citation-string guards -- those are correct and
would report OK on both mutations.
Set file added 2026-08-24, after the record itself. The mutations are
taken verbatim from its own table; nothing here is a new claim.
Run:  python3 scripts/mutate.py --set docs/mutations/adr-0163-front-page-pair.json

mutations._claimed: caught by the front-page test, which runs the resolver
mutations._note: 0.398 is the other candidate row on the same page under the same reference. check_citations_match_their_enzyme reports OK on this, correctly -- the value does occur on the page. Only the pairing is wrong, and only the resolver knows the pairing.

mutations.description: right value, a real reference belonging to the other row: 286469 -> 286442
mutations._claimed: caught by the front-page test, which runs the resolver
mutations._note: 286442 is a genuine LDH reference, so every string-matching guard passes. The resolver returns 286469 for this substrate and organism, and nothing short of running it can tell the two apart.
